<reason>Side A won by demonstrating that the proposition collapses into either redundancy with existing law or absurdity when applied to unscripted influencer content. Side A's pressure questions exposed Side B retreating from "broadcast strictness" (B2.3) to "clear notice when sponsored content begins" (B4.4), which existing consumer protection law already requires. While Side B effectively argued functional equivalence and parasocial trust, they failed to articulate a coherent standard distinct from current law that wouldn't duplicate existing rules or trigger the disclosure fatigue Side A warned of.</reason>
